claims.text: The magnetocaloric response of as-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy-alloy films or nanoribbons is governed by inherent magnetic anisotropy.
The magnetocaloric response of these nanostructures is governed by their dimensional constraints.
Heat-transfer-rate limitations govern the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis during magnetic-cooling cycles.
Varying the frequency of controlled low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles is the proposed intervention.
Nanoscale films or patterned nanoribbons will have a reduced magnetocaloric response relative to bulk forms.
Nanoscale films or patterned nanoribbons will exhibit increased hysteresis relative to bulk forms.
The maximum usable cycle frequency will be limited by heat-transfer rate.
The proposed mechanism is an interplay among magnetic anisotropy, dimensional constraints, and heat-transfer-rate limitations.
The hypothesis is intended to apply under low applied fields and in a genuinely low-dimensional state.
Bulk as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloy is the comparison baseline.
Failure to observe a significant reduction in magnetocaloric response relative to bulk would falsify the prediction of reduced response.
Failure to find cycle frequency limited by heat-transfer rate would falsify the heat-transfer-limitation claim.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome states that hysteresis increases relative to bulk, whereas the falsification rule treats hysteresis not being reduced relative to bulk as a falsifying result. The expected direction of the hysteresis change is therefore inconsistent.
